textbookText: Chapter 14 Reflection at Curved Mirror Born in Darmstadt, Germany on May 12, 1803, Justus von Liebig received his doctorate from the University of Erlangen in Bavaria in 1822. Justus von Liebig was a chemist, who is widely credited as one of the founders of agricultural chemistry. He made crucial contributions to the analysis of organic compounds, and, in his early years, also published several works on the use of inorganic fertilizers in several languages. He discovered that nitrogen was an essential plant nutrient, and presented his famous Law of the Minimum which explained the effect of individual nutrients on crops.

A discovery by Liebig in 1835 made mirrors widely available. Liebig found a way to coat glass with a thin layer of metallic silver by depositing the metal directly by means of a chemical reaction. [Justus von Liebig, 1803-1873]

Do you know? Convex mirrors are used in vehicles for rear view but not concave mirrors. 14.1 Introduction Reflection of light is the fundamental concept in the study of optics and visual perception. When light travelling through one medium approaches to the surface of another medium, it is partly reflected, partly absorbed, and the remaining part is transmitted. "The phenomenon of coming back of light in the same medium when it strikes on a surface is known as reflection of light." The bouncing off of the light occurs in a predictable manner as it follows the laws of reflection. Generally, light reflects from reflecting surfaces (plane, polished, smooth shiny surfaces, etc.) like plane mirrors, curved mirrors, etc. The reflection of light from plane mirrors and curved mirrors produces an image of an object. The working of optical instruments is based on the reflection of light. The understanding of the principles of reflection of light is very important in many aspects of the physical world around us from the functioning of our eyes to the behavior of astronomical objects. In this chapter, we will explore the properties and applications of reflected light establishing a found ation for further studies in physics and applied sciences. 14.2 Image When the reflected rays meet or appear at a point, then the image of an object is formed. There are two types of images. They are real images and virtual images.
